s: Auxiliary process co-located with the main application container handling cross-cutting concerns like networking, logging, and security.
w: Deployed as a second container in the same pod (Kubernetes) or process group, the sidecar intercepts inbound/outbound traffic transparently. It handles mTLS termination, retries, circuit breaking, metrics collection, and log shipping so application code stays clean. Service mesh data planes (Envoy, linkerd-proxy) are the canonical sidecars. Shared network namespace means localhost communication with zero latency overhead.
use: Service mesh proxy: mTLS, retries, traffic splitting without app changes
Log shipping agent forwarding container stdout to aggregator
Metrics exporter collecting runtime stats for Prometheus scraping
Database proxy (PgBouncer sidecar) managing connection pooling per pod
avoid: Single-container simple deployments where sidecar overhead exceeds benefit
Performance-critical paths where sidecar hop latency is unacceptable
Teams without Kubernetes or process-management capacity to operate sidecar lifecycle

pat.d: Sidecars form the data plane; mesh control plane configures them centrally.

pits: Sidecar upgrade storms rolling across every pod simultaneously - canary node pools
Resource contention with app container when both compete for CPU/memory - set explicit limits
tips: The pattern name is sidecar; the application is the front car
Ambient mesh (no sidecar) is emerging - mention awareness for forward-looking answers
